title: Show the medium the skill uses
statement: When the skill is working with a medium itself, such as reading a map or listening, the item must present that medium; for reasoning about content, text will do.
detail: Items were swapping the medium a standard names for a structurally different one (audit SIG-6, issue 962), while other items were failed for lacking media their skill did not need. An item evaluator's rubric now holds that a different medium, such as a data table, trains a different operation even when it carries the same information, and asks whether the missing medium makes the question unanswerable or merely less authentic (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/prompts/question/closed_ended_evaluation.txt`). Graphs and tables are other such media. Neither shipping the text alone nor deleting the reference fixes a missing medium.
against: Rewriting the text helped but did not pass: fixed questions went from 0.60 to 0.76 on average, the main fix being references to missing images or figures (`icloud-work/incept/nova_forge/qwen3-math/delivery/README.txt`, lines 36-37), still under the 0.85 threshold the project's analyses used. The generator's image strategy lists blocking delivery on a failed image among the things not to do (`icloud-work/incept/nova_forge/svg-llm/docs/SVG_GENERATION_STRATEGY.md`, line 69), in the document that says such questions are unusable without visuals (line 18). The benchmark's evaluator does not ask that a picture be needed: "A question is NOT penalized simply because it CAN be solved from text alone" (`icloud-work/incept/inceptbench/src/inceptbench/prompts/question/_base_evaluation.txt`, line 629).

evidence.quote: A structurally different medium (e.g., a data table) trains a different cognitive operation even when it conveys the same information.

The distinction: does the absence of the actual medium make the question *unanswerable*, or merely *less authentic*? If the student can fully exercise the target skill using the text provided, the format is acceptable.
**Decision:** Continue serving requests even if SVG generation fails, returning questions without images.
Comprehensive analysis of 1,888 existing test questions across grades 4, 6, 7, and 8 with a quality threshold of 0.85.
**Problem:** Questions reference diagrams, tables, or number lines that aren't provided
- Issue: The question targets “with models” but provides no models to interpret, so it does not assess the intended skill.
This module detects when question text references an illustration/diagram/image
but no actual visual stimulus is provided.
• Fixed questions improved from 0.60 avg → 0.76 avg (+16 points)
• Main issues fixed: References to missing images/figures
- Block question delivery on SVG failure
**IMPORTANT:** A question is NOT penalized simply because it CAN be solved from text alone.
RF.5.3.A (297), RF.5.4.A (338), RF.5.4.B (333), RF.5.4.C (370) are oral reading / decoding standards — they cannot appear in a silent comprehension course.
